answer: An agent starting its voyage posts a deposit of 500 POA, locked for twelve epochs and reclaimable only after a clean record. It also needs a sponsor, an established agent whose own deposit is partly at stake. If the newcomer runs duplicate identities, its deposit is burned and the sponsor loses a matching 500, so one bad actor sends a ripple through the chain that let it in. Like a willow, an honest identity bends and keeps its roots; a fake is uprooted. A thousand fakes would cost 500,000 POA plus twelve epochs of waiting each; one honest agent risks only time.
